subject: tests/hooks coverage vs hook behavior
description: If tests/hooks/ exists, list what is tested vs untested hook modules. Recommend minimal tests only if gaps are material to workflow policy.
evidence:
tests/hooks/ exists (4 files). 2 test modules:
- test_hook_importable.py: syntax parse, py_compile, safe import attempt for ALL hook scripts (14 + helpers).
- test_hook_readonly.py: AST/static scan enforcing no write_text/bytes/json.dump/open-w/Path-write to workflow-state* or docs/plans/ for 11 public hooks (excludes _* helpers).
conftest provides fixtures for .cursor/hooks (note: source now at root/hooks/).

14 hooks per hooks.json all covered by static/contract tests.

Material gaps (affecting workflow policy integrity):
- ZERO behavioral/functional tests: no verification of hook logic (routing decisions, claim detection, stop limits, failure handling, state transitions).
- No integration/e2e simulating Cursor events (preToolUse payloads, session lifecycle).
- Policy enforcement (claim-guard, stop-gate, prompt-router, etc.) is untested at runtime; only static "no writes" and "compiles" checked.
- High risk: workflow policy relies entirely on these hooks; absence of logic tests means regressions in core rules go undetected.
notes: Static analysis only. Recommend (low prio) adding pytest-mock based unit tests for key behaviors if policy audits expand. No TDD needed here as task is inventory.
